summary: Range-light station at the southern entrance to the Strait of Canso: a light from 1851 or 1852, a tower of 1895, the last lighthouse removed in 2003, and two range lights in its place.

structures.name: Eddy Point Lighthouse (fibreglass tower)
structures.note: Bolted to a concrete slab in 1988; lit 1989 per NSLPS; removed by the Coast Guard in 2003.

access.note: Reached by car along Marine Drive, per the Nova Scotia Lighthouse Preservation Society.

visit.note: No lighthouse stands on the point; the modern range lights can be seen from it.

events.note: NSLPS: year lit 1851. Lighthouse Friends: work began 1851 and the light went into service in 1852 (see resolved_conflicts).
New tower built against the east side of the old light by T. M. Crowe of Truro for $800; placed in operation 1 January 1895.
Edward Mundell appointed 28 July 1903 (Department staff table).
Fifth-order dioptric lens and hand fog horn (NSLPS).
Diaphone fog alarm in a building attached to the light (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS puts the diaphone in operation in 1930.
Combined dwelling and lighthouse (Lighthouse Friends); NSLPS calls it the third tower.
Fire destroyed the 1929 building, per Lighthouse Friends only; NSLPS does not record a fire and keeps the 1929 tower until 1989.
Reduced to one keeper in 1977 and de-staffed in 1979 after remote monitoring from the Eddy Point Traffic Centre (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS: automated by 1979.
Circular fibreglass tower, bolted to a slab in 1988 (Lighthouse Friends); NSLPS dates the light to 1989.
Fibreglass tower removed by the Coast Guard.
Pair of range lights set up on the point to guide ships through the strait (Lighthouse Friends; CCG List of Lights).

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends and the Nova Scotia Lighthouse Preservation Society both say the fibreglass tower was removed by the Coast Guard in 2003, and that the point now carries range lights, not a lighthouse.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1851 is the year the Nova Scotia society gives as lit. Lighthouse Friends says work began in 1851 and the light went into service in 1852 (a Nova Scotia lighthouse guide also says 1852). The story gives both years and does not choose.

The record's 1989 comes from the Lighthouse Directory. Lighthouse Friends dates the bolting of the fibreglass tower to a slab in 1988, and the society lists the light as lit in 1989. The story uses 1989 for lighting and notes 1988.

The record's light data (Oc G 11s, 11.9 m focal height) describe the Coast Guard's front range light, which is a different structure from the old lighthouse. The story treats the characteristic as the present range light's.
The narrative gives 1863 (LHF text: 'placed in charge of the light in 1863'); LHF's keeper list gives 1864 to 1869. The story states both.

The 1904 report's keeper list (year ended 30 June 1903) already names Edward Mundell at Eddy Point, but the 1910 staff table gives his appointment as 28 July 1903, which falls in the following fiscal year. The story states both records; the list is probably compiled after the fiscal year closed.

notes_for_editor: 1) Long Eddy Point (New Brunswick, a fog alarm) is a different station and must not be merged with this record. 2) NSLPS lists a keeper, Jim Guptill, at Eddy Point for 1987-1988; Lighthouse Friends does not, and it gives a Jim Guptill at Gull Rock from 1974. The story notes the disagreement; the NSLPS entry is unconfirmed. 3) The Department's keeper tables are OCR text with columns printed in blocks. Edward Mundell's name and the 28 July 1903 date were matched by position in the same row (scan pages 167 and 231); both page images were checked: the 1904 report (scan 231, printed p. 218) shows the row Mundell, Edward / Eddy Point / July 28, 1903, and the 1910 staff table (scan 167, printed p. 160) shows Eddy Point / Edward Mundell / July 28, 1903. The fiscal-year label of the 1904 report (ended June 30, 1903) was checked in the corpus text. 4) No primary source read here covers 1851-1895 (the Department's annual reports in the corpus start in 1900), so the first light and the 1893-95 tower rest on Lighthouse Friends and the NSLPS. 5) Ownership of the point is not stated in the sources read, so the record's ownership 'unknown' stays. 6) Not used: a 1908 Department line on 'Eddy point, retaining wall' in an uncertain section (scan 77, p. 68); 1908 'Fortuna ... Ashore in Strait of Canso' (scan 43, p. 34) and a 1924 trawler wreck 'at the south entrance of Strait of Canso', neither tied to Eddy Point in the text.
